**Acid-Base Balance**

**9.1 Demonstrating Properties of Dilute Acids through Experiments**

(i) **Taste:**
All dilute acids are sour in taste. We have already seen that the acidic foods are sour. However, remain careful not to taste any acid in the laboratory. If your tongue comes in contact with any of these acids, they will instantly corrode your tongue. You may try the taste of tamarind instead which will tell you tartaric acid tastes sour.

(ii) **Corrosive:**
Acids are corrosive. If you put a piece of metal in acid, the outer edge of the metal will be corroded.

(iii) **Litmus Test:**
Acid turns blue litmus into red. Take 2-3 mL hydrochloric acid in a test tube and add a blue litmus to it. You will see, the blue colour will turn red.
